findings.claim: The shared `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` guard removes ExcludeFromCodeCoverage from every class generated into a .NET Framework project. ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute is available on the supported .NET Framework versions, so this is not the acceptance criterion's permitted conditional omission for targets where the attribute is unavailable; generated formatters and resolvers remain undecorated there, contrary to the requirement that all generated code be decorated. The same guard is repeated in the other templates.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.NetFrameworkExcludeFromCodeCoverageTests.AllGeneratedTypesAreDecoratedOnNetFramework. It runs the generator with NETFRAMEWORK defined and requires every generated class to retain ExcludeFromCodeCoverage; head omits the attribute and fails the test.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Decorate every generated formatter and resolver type, including generated cache and formatter-lookup helper classes, without adding any generator setting; conditionally omit the attribute only on targets where it cannot be used. This is the scope implemented by the template changes, apart from the .NET Framework omission identified above.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Read the requested scope as generated formatter classes only: decorate integer-key, string-key, enum, and union formatters while leaving resolver and helper classes unchanged, and add an opt-out generator option that suppresses the formatter attribute when requested.
